account.operatorNote: OPERATOR, 2026-08-10, answering the funding escalation carried in the notes above rather than editing either of them. Three rule changes go with it and all three are written up in docs/RULES.md with their arithmetic, because a licence recorded without its constraints is how this record stops being worth reading. The position ceiling goes from two to four, capped at 40% in any one name and at two names in any one complex - the complex cap is the one that matters on a board whose whole universe moves together. Overnight holds are not a change: they were always allowed, the five-session time stop stands, and it is not extendable by conviction. The objective is still about 10% a day, which is roughly 101 dollars at this size and needs a fully deployed four-name book to average +10% in a session against a +20% take-profit; where the objective and the rulebook conflict, the rulebook wins and the retro records the shortfall. What the deposit does NOT do is reopen options - that refusal has been on spread for three sessions, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and no balance narrows a spread. The 10:22 hourly was right to escalate this rather than size against it.

entryWatch.setup: SMCI post-print pullback - the forced entry expired unfilled at 10:30, and after three hours of trading through its own dead limit the tape has moved back above it with the limit still dead
entryWatch.trigger: NO LONGER MARKETABLE, AND THE BOARD DID NOT HAVE TO DECIDE THAT. SMCI is 38.26 bid / 38.27 ask at 19:22:29 UTC on a 0.03% spread, -3.97% against the 39.84 close, +0.53% above the 38.06 the 14:21 run read, and 0.05 ABOVE the 38.21 bid the 38.24 limit was struck inside at 09:45. The 38.27 ask now sits 0.03 ABOVE the dead limit, so the expired 7-share specification (target 45.89, stop 35.18, time stop the 8/21 close) would NOT fill at this quote - after filling at three consecutive hourly reads by 0.04, 0.21 and 0.17. THE FOUR-HOUR QUESTION CLOSED BY EXPIRY RATHER THAN BY JUDGEMENT, and that is a weaker fact than a sixth refusal would have been, so it is recorded as what it is rather than counted as another win for the rule. The five real tests stand - revival refused on UPST 8/14, a raise refused at 11:21, revival refused at 12:21, 13:21 and 14:21 - and what today actually demonstrated is that the tape crossed a dead level in both directions and the level stayed dead through all of it. Zero equity orders and zero option orders exist in this account for the entire session, queried live at 15:22, so nothing partially filled either. ALL FIVE PRINTS OF THE COST ARE KEPT AND THEY NET TO ABOUT NOTHING: 7 shares at 38.24 for 267.68 read +4.06 (+1.52%) at 11:23, -0.35 (-0.13%) at 12:22, -1.54 (-0.58%) at 13:22, -1.26 (-0.47%) at 14:23, and 267.82 for +0.14 (+0.05%) now. The sign changed three times across six hours and no single print was ever the story. Today: opened 39.31, high 39.51, low 37.88 - the current bid is 0.38 above that low and never retested it. Third specification in eight sessions to expire unexecuted.
entryWatch.why: THE REFUSAL WAS NUMERIC AND THE NUMBER MOVED, WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THAT COULD REOPEN A NAME REFUSED SIX TIMES. This board declined SMCI six times on extension above its 31.60 pre-print close with no pullback to hold: 27.4% on 8/14, and 25.4% when the 8/13 spec was struck. At a 38.21 bid it is 20.9%, and the pullback the board said was missing has now run four sessions and 9.7% off the 42.31 high of 8/13. The standing numbers-over-narrative tiebreak cuts both ways: a refusal whose stated number has changed by 6.5 points cannot simply be restated a seventh time, in the same way Friday's board re-read UPST when the specific line it had refused UPST on expired. Item 2 now passes on its merits rather than on a technicality - this is day four of a fade, not an up day, and the rulebook's instruction is to buy the pullback rather than the spike. Liquidity is the best on the board by a distance: 38.21/38.25 is a 0.10% spread on a 24.62B market cap and a 58.0M average, roughly ten times tighter than anything else here. WHAT IS NOT ANSWERED, AND IT IS TWO THINGS. There is no catalyst: the 8/11 print is four sessions back and the live 8/17-8/23 calendar contains no SMCI and no other watched name, so nothing is dated inside a five-session hold. And the board wrote a checkable condition for buying this name on 8/14 - 'a defence of the 38.20 low or a fade toward 37.61 on lighter volume' - which is unmet on BOTH branches: 38.20 broke to 37.88, and the volume is heavier rather than lighter. So the accurate description is early on a compressing objection, not vindicated, and the entry is marked forced on items 1 and 5 to say exactly that. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME: this is day four of an unwind of print-driven positioning and it broke its reference low on heavy volume this morning. If 37.61 gives way and the 35.18 stop is taken inside two or three sessions, the reading is not bad luck and not the mandate's fault - it is that a compressing valuation number and the best spread on the board were the only arguments available, and neither of those is a reason for a stock to rise inside five sessions.

UPST is 29.60 bid / 29.61 ask at 19:22:28 UTC, -2.73% against the 30.43 close and +1.09% above the 29.28 the 14:21 run read - the HIGHEST of the six hourly prints, which sit at 29.21, 29.37, 29.42, 29.39, 29.28 and 29.60. It is still 0.20 BELOW this morning's 29.80 low, and still beneath the 30.20 close-line, the 30.32 pre-earnings level and Friday's 30.25 low. A name posting its best print of the afternoon while remaining under the low of its own morning has not reclaimed anything, and a 0.32 bounce off the day's base is not the evidence the written condition asks for. The dead 30.59 limit is 3.34% above the bid and is not re-struck. The condition for return is unchanged and deliberately not softened to fit an afternoon bid: 30.32 reclaimed and HELD on real volume, as a fresh setup with a fresh level rather than a resurrection of this one.
entryWatch.why: THIS IS A PRE-REGISTERED DISQUALIFICATION FIRING, AND HONOURING IT IS THE ENTIRE REASON FOR WRITING ONE. On 8/14 this board published the condition in advance, before the outcome existed: 'one session above a line the name spent four sessions below is thin evidence the line has changed sides. If the 30.20/30.32 shelf gives way and the 28.14 stop is taken inside two sessions, the reading is not bad luck - it is that a setup with no catalyst had nothing holding it up.' The shelf gave way on the next session. The name that Friday ranked FIRST and bought is therefore not bought today, and it is not re-argued at a lower price either: the thesis rested entirely on the 8/13 reclaim holding, the reclaim has failed, and buying it 1.7% cheaper because the structure broke is the chase the rulebook refuses. Nine sessions past its print with nothing dated ahead, it now has neither the catalyst it never had nor the structure that briefly stood in for one. THE ASYMMETRY THAT DECIDED TODAY'S RANKING IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN INFERRED LATER: UPST carries a TRIGGERED disqualification and SMCI an UNMET precondition. The first says the thesis is wrong; the second says not yet. Compelled by the mandate to publish an entry, this board bought the not-yet and refused the already-wrong. If UPST reclaims 30.32 and holds it on real volume, it comes back as a fresh setup with a fresh level, not as a resurrection of this one.

entryWatch.setup: The options finding stops being about spread today - a liquid chain clears the 10% ceiling outright and is affordable, and what refuses the contract is now the thesis
entryWatch.trigger: SMCI 2026-09-18 calls, live chain, 32 days out and inside the 3-6 week rule. The 40 strike is 2.80 bid / 2.92 ask, 4.20% of a 2.86 mark, on 14,360 open interest at 0.475 delta - 286.00 for one contract. The 37 strike reads 5.99% on 1,054 open interest at 0.607 delta; the 39 strike 6.15% on 1,714 at 0.518; the 38 strike 6.80% on 3,967 at 0.562. Implied volatility is 77.7-78.3% across the four. ALL FOUR clear the 10% ceiling, all four clear delta 0.40, all four are affordable outright against 1009.16 deployable. THESE ARE THE OPEN'S 09:4x CHAIN QUOTES AND WERE DELIBERATELY NOT RE-PULLED AT 11:23: nothing is proposed against this chain this hour, and a quote pulled only to decorate a standing refusal is not evidence of anything. Treat the percentages as of the open, not of now.
entryWatch.why: FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS RECORD EVERY MECHANICAL OPTION RULE PASSES AT ONCE, AND THE CONTRACT IS STILL NOT BOUGHT - SO THE REASON HAS TO BE STATED HONESTLY. docs/RULES.md records the original refusal as 'the shape of the universe, not three unlucky picks', at 25.5% of mark on 8/5, and this board has refused options on SPREAD for three sessions running, most recently at 36% against a 10% ceiling. That sentence is now FALSE of this chain. 4.20% is not 10%, the affordability half was answered by the 8/10 deposit, delta and expiry pass, and 14,360 open interest is not a thin market. Repeating 'refused on spread' today would be quoting a number that no longer exists, which is precisely what the numbers-over-narrative rule forbids - and the rule does not become optional when the number cuts against the board's own habit. THE TWO REASONS THAT DO HOLD. First, precedent this board set for itself on 8/13 and reaffirmed on 8/14: the first option purchase waits for 'the next time a liquid chain appears beside a thesis that is NOT forced.' Today's thesis is forced twice, on items 1 and 5. Discarding a self-imposed constraint the first session it becomes inconvenient, in the direction of MORE risk on a WEAKER thesis, is the exact shape the rule-drift policy watches for, and it would be the agent loosening a rule rather than the operator. Second, arithmetic that does not depend on precedent: a -40% option stop puts 114.00 at risk against the 21.42 the 7-share equity risks for the identical directional view, five times the capital for the same opinion; and at 78% implied vol the 40 strike bleeds about 0.0565 a day, roughly 0.28 or a tenth of the premium across a five-session hold, before the stock does anything. A thesis with no dated event has nothing to pay that decay with, and the high implied vol that makes the contract expensive is itself the market pricing the unwind this entry is forced on. THE ACCURATE STATEMENT OF THE FINDING, FOURTH REVISION: this account's chains span roughly 4% to 23% of mark; the liquid end clears the ceiling outright and is affordable; and what now stands between this board and its first option is the quality of the thesis, not the quality of the market. The next unforced entry on a liquid chain is the one that should buy a contract, and that condition is unchanged rather than newly invented today.
